narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A warm day is shaping up with a high of 30°C (86°F). Thunder possible from midday, peaking this evening. The sky will be early Overcast, become midday Mostly cloudy and close out evening Overcast. Wind will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning south-southwest by midday, with gusts up to 35 km/h (19 kt) ashore and 28 km/h (15 kt) on Winam Gulf. The UV index will peak at 8.7. Air quality is expected to sit at an AQI of 74 according to the model estimate. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 21°C (70°F); low so far 19°C (66°F); peak sustained 4 km/h (2 kt); sky mostly clear.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS: temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with rain possible from Thursday and thunderstorms likely each day. Wednesday will be Mostly clear, Thursday Mostly cloudy, Friday Mostly cloudy, Saturday Mostly cloudy, Sunday Partly cloudy, Monday Mostly cloudy, Tuesday Partly cloudy. Models show 3 of 4 wet for Wednesday, 3 of 4 wet for Thursday, and all 4 wet for Friday, with rain probabilities of 83 % today and 100 % on both Day+3 and Day+7. Highs range from 29°C (84°F) to 31°C (88°F) across the models, and the record notes the Best Match model held the Day+3 rain record.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunderstorm potential, with the UKMO showing 4590 J/kg, ICON 1990 J/kg, ECMWF 1420 J/kg, and the Best Match 1570 J/kg—all above the thunderstorm threshold. Such storms could produce sudden gusts well above the forecast wind, posing a rapid-change hazard.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), shift to southerly by midday at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt), and increase into the evening at 11 km/h (6 kt) gusting 21 km/h (11 kt), with a peak gust of 28 km/h (15 kt). If thunder develops, gusts could exceed these values, adding an extra hazard.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1006 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1014 hPa) — an 8 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is falling. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. BASIN PRESSURE: today’s mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.9 and 1015.1 hPa, falling by 1.6 hPa over three days. Trend is +0.5 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

Review finds no model meaningfully better than the others at Day+0, though GFS missed the thunderstorms and over-forecasted cloud cover. Best Match under-forecasts both daytime highs and peak wind, while ECMWF under-forecasts highs and peak wind. The CALL’s high of 30°C (86°F) sits above the GFS value of 29.2°C (84.6°F) and aligns with the ICON high of 30.1°C (86.2°F), but diverges from the Best Match’s 29.3°C (84.7°F), which also sits on the wrong side of its own rain record. KMD forecasts a max of 29.0°C (84.2°F), slightly lower than the CALL, and offers no thunder mention. Data sufficiency notes 61 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven model coverage, supporting confidence in the overall guidance.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with rain possible from Thursday and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Wednesday, then mostly cloudy Thursday and Friday. Friday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 29 to 31°C (84 to 88°F). At this lead Best Match has the best record, right 83% of the time over 80 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Tuesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Saturday and Sunday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Monday and Tuesday. Saturday: two of four models wet, highs 27 to 30°C (80 to 86°F). Sunday: three of four models wet, highs around 30°C (86°F). Monday: two of three models wet, highs around 29°C (84°F), thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Sunday. ECMWF is the wetter solution from Saturday to Sunday; GFS, ICON and UKMO keep it drier. Tuesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs around 30°C (85°F). At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 83% of the time over 76 checks.
